A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ECVC and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D. Text and rendered-page comparisons support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original rate-distortion experiments, complexity measurements and ablations in Section 4, with additional ECVC and ECVC-FM results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v4 retains original rate-distortion experiments, complexity measurements and ablations in Section 4 and additional experimental results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The two-reference context mining, multi-head linear cross attention and partial cascaded finetuning procedures are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same ECVC-FM variant.

E1.justification: Both versions use Vimeo-90K and BVI-DVC for training and finetuning, and HEVC B–E, UVG and MCL-JCV for evaluation. No dataset, task or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including the DCVC variants, reproduced DCVC-DC baseline and VTM-13.2 anchor. The appendix comparisons are also retained unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix C retain the same training settings, RGB conversion, distortion metrics, codec configuration and evaluation protocols using IP 32 or -1 with 96 or all frames.

E4.justification: The component and model-size ablations, finetuning-length analysis, Gaussian-noise perturbation, reconstruction examples and attention visualizations remain unchanged in Tables 6–7 and Figures 5, 8–9.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added, removed or revised.

E6.justification: All experimental tables, plots and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, ECVC's average BD-Rate remains -29.3% in Table 1 under IP 32 with 96 frames and -32.1% in Table 4 under IP -1 with all frames.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, its attention-normalization proof, the complexity derivations and Equations 1–9 retain the same mathematical content. Changes around them are text reflow.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about exploiting non-local correlations, mitigating accumulated errors and achieving state-of-the-art compression performance.

C2.justification: The explanations of error propagation, longer-sequence finetuning and attention behavior are unchanged. The conclusion retains the out-of-domain anime limitation and proposed future instance-adaptive optimization.

D1.justification: v3's abstract states that ECVC code is available and provides a repository link; v4 removes both without replacement elsewhere. Other implementation and reproduction details remain unchanged. This establishes reduced access information, without establishing a change in actual code availability.

R1.justification: The same 66 references and research positioning are retained. Reference 26's citation-page backlink changes because its citing text moves across a page boundary.

P1.justification: v4 updates an author email address and the arXiv version/date stamp and deletes the abstract's code-availability sentence. The remaining wording, section order and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The shortened abstract causes limited column and page-break reflow across pages 1–4, including equation placement. All figures, tables and captions retain their content and design; experimental and appendix pages render identically.

improvement.justification: The scientific content and appendix evidence are unchanged, but v4 removes the sole explicit ECVC code-availability statement and repository pointer. This modestly weakens implementation discoverability and reproducibility documentation, with no substantive compensating improvement. The PDFs do not establish whether the repository itself remains available.
